test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 July 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In what time does a sum of money amount to twice of itself at simple interest of 10% per annum?
solution:
Given:

Rate of interest = 10%

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Let's suppose, Rs. P will be twice itself in T years.

According to the concept,

P + (P × 10 × T)/100 = 2P

⇒ (P × 10 × T)/100 = 2P - P

⇒ (P × 10 × T)/100 = P

⇒ T = 10 (∵ P ≠ 0)

**∴ In 10 years, a sum of money will amount to twice of itself at simple interest of 10% per annum.**
